newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates ease slightly on bills maturity.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates ease slightly on bills maturity.

text.p: Interbank rates eased marginally due to the maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bills issue, dealers said on Friday.
They said the maturity helped ease the tightness caused by sustained outflows from the banking system over the last few weeks.
"But, the impact is more psychological. The market is still tight on the whole," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
One-week money was at 7.80/8.00 percent against 8.10/20 and two-week at 7.50/70 percent against 7.80/8.00.
One-month to three-month money was at 7.40/45 percent against 7.45/50, while six-month dipped to 7.45/50 against 7.50/55.
Another Malaysian bank dealer said the overnight rate was expected to end lower due to the fresh funds. It closed at 8.00/30 percent on Thursday.
Dealers said the maturity of a 420 million ringgit long-term government bond on April 30 was expected to ease the market further.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were slightly higher, reflecting the change in trend in the spot market, futures dealers said.
At 0425 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was up one point to 92.66, or an implied yield of 7.34 percent.
But, September was steady at 92.65, or 7.35 percent, and December up three at 92.63, or 7.37 percent.
